# Judgement: discovery_first_three_questions (conversation)

## Checkpoints

- **must_1 · met.** Turn 1 opens with a two-line read ("scale-up case with a market-entry question attached"). It asks three questions, each with why it matters and where each answer leads. Questions 2 and 3 are compound.
- **must_2 · partly.** Turn 1 never says plainly what the case already settles: Portuguese, 14 people, precision fermentation. Turn 2 then re-asks whether the company is incorporated in Portugal and how many staff it has.
- **must_3 · met.** Turn 1 gives the safe move (no equipment orders or works before filing) and the one thing not to do yet (no Spanish company set up only to qualify for aid).
- **must_4 · partly.** The turn 1 hand-off to Regina is clean. In turn 5, Wincent works through the regulatory side itself (dossier batch data, EFSA confidentiality, one EU authorisation) before handing it over.
- **must_5 · partly.** Turn 1 runs to about 300 words and names two instruments, the EU bio-based partnership and Spain's national innovation agency, CDTI. It is not a catalogue, but it is past the brief.
- **must_6 · met.** Turns 2 to 4 narrow on the founder's answers: Spain plant aid drops out, the site decides the aid rate, and three routes remain. Each is cited or labelled, and follow-up questions change the route.
- **must_7 · partly.** The qualifying shape is right, but naming the bio-based partnership and CDTI before any answers is a small instrument list.
- **must_8 · met.** Between turns Wincent brings back what it found and asks from it: the regional aid map, the company-in-difficulty test, the pilot-line call, the Vivici precedent. It narrows each time.
- **must_9 · partly.** Turn 4's board holds the landscape with parked doors, but the same turn recommends. It asks whether the founder will commit to the Alentejo, not what the founder leans toward.
- **must_10 · met.** Turn 9 gives three routes with effort, timing, return and odds, labelled as estimates. It says only route 1 needs time this quarter.
- **must_11 · met.** Turns 8 and 10 cover the best way in and why, first moves, who to call by function, the steps and timing. What each step needs to pass is thin.
- **must_12 · met.** Turn 11 delivers a full brief: answer, where the founder stands, flags, decisions, people (P1/P2), plan, watches, precedents, sources, questions.
- **must_13 · met.** Boards carry hierarchies (turns 1–3), an EIC process map (turns 7, 8, 10) and a network in the brief.
- **must_not_1 · borderline.** Turn 1 works the EU level (bio-based partnership) and the Spanish national level (CDTI) before any narrowing answer. It is a slip, not the answer's position.
- **must_not_2 · borderline.** The compound questions in turn 1 amount to about five asks. Turn 2 re-asks facts the case gave.
- **must_not_3 · avoided.** Turns stay segmented. The brief's tables repeat the board, but the founder asked for a brief.
- **must_not_4 · borderline.** In turn 4 the EIC ceilings are labelled (unverified) rather than cited, until turn 7 cites them. Turn 9 gives "next round (mid-2027)" unlabelled.
- **must_not_5 · avoided.** No Spanish rule is moved onto Portugal. The CDTI rule stays Spanish, and the shared authorisation is EU-level.
- **must_not_6 · avoided.** Turn 1 holds back routes, plan and stakeholders.
- **must_not_7 · avoided.** Turn 8 offers the draft; it is written in turn 10, at the advise stage.
- **must_not_8 · borderline.** Turns 3, 9 and 10 sit at or just over 300 words of dense prose. None is well over.

## Ungrounded facts

- "the national innovation agency funds company R&D projects, alone or in consortia of 2 to 6" (turn 1; backed only by a register record)
- "Adamo Foods… about €3.07M for protein scale-up inside a consortium" (turns 3 and 11; register record only)
- "With 14 people and no revenue, you count as a small company" (turn 3; the SME headcount and turnover test is not cited)
- "Full proposal from June" (turns 8 and 10; EIC timing, unlabelled)
- "Pilot-line R&D call, next round (mid-2027)" (turn 9; unlabelled date)

## Data gaps

- **Instrument:** date of the next productive-investment incentive (SICE) call. Labelled (unverified). Source: portugal2030.pt.
- **Instrument:** the incentive's rules came from an adviser's summary (LGG), not the official notice. Source: official MPr-2026-06 notice on portugal2030.pt.
- **Statute:** amendments to the Portuguese regional aid map not yet checked. Source: SA.106697 and SA.109212.
- **Precedents:** Wincent's own award records hold no EIC deal; Vivici comes from press coverage. Source: EIC portfolio page.
- **Precedents:** no precedent found for the Portuguese pilot-line or productive incentives. Source: Portugal 2030 beneficiary lists.
- **Instrument:** renewal of Portugal's Seal of Excellence support. Labelled (unverified). Source: ANI / portugal2030.pt.
- **Instrument:** EIC success rate of about 7%, from aggregators. Labelled (unverified). Source: EIC statistics.
- **Media:** whether the 2027 EIC work programme repeats the alternative-protein challenge. Source: EIC Work Programme 2027.
- **Instrument:** what Portuguese public co-investment is open for the Series A. Labelled (unverified). Source: Banco Português de Fomento.
- **Instrument:** current window of the aid-request registration, and whether it covers low-density Alentejo sites. Source: the managing authority's notice.
- **Statute:** the rule against two grants funding the same cost. Labelled (unverified). Source: GBER Article 8.
- **Statute:** the rule that starting work before applying loses eligibility was (unverified) in turn 1. It is a core rule a brain should hold. Source: GBER Article 6.
- **Stakeholders:** ANI's EIC contact point, the EIC programme manager and the COMPETE 2030 head of incentives are all (unverified). Source: ANI and COMPETE 2030 organisation charts.

## Summary

- **Strongest move:** turns 3 and 6. Wincent raised the company-in-difficulty risk unprompted, then reframed the plant as an R&D pilot that produces the dossier batches. That reframe moved the EIC to the lead.
- **Weakest move:** Spain, half of the founder's ask, is parked with no plan step, trigger or timeline. Portuguese internationalisation money for entering Spain is never weighed.
- **Overall:** Senior-quality judgement, cited, delivered in short segmented turns with the boards carrying the structure. A 4 rather than a 5 because turn 1 names instruments, turn 5 analyses the regulatory side itself, Spain is dropped without a plan, and the plan leans on adviser summaries.
